title: The deploy that ate the heap

author.name: Sample staff engineer
author.note: Example mod written for the MVP

story: You are on call for the orders API, a JVM service on 4 pods. Traffic is a normal Tuesday. CI deploys several times a day and nobody watches the deploys closely. Something will go wrong; your job is to notice, find out why, and fix it with the least damage.

timeline.deploy: orders-api v2.14.0 rolled out by ci-bot ("add per-request audit context")

timeline.message: Seeing some slow queries alerts from the DB side, anything changed on your end?
Order confirmations are slow for EU customers, is something going on?

runbook.title: What changed?
runbook.detail: Most incidents follow a change. Look at the deploy markers on the graphs before anything else.

runbook.title: Read the heap graph as a slope, not a level
runbook.detail: A heap that only goes up between deploys is a leak. GC pauses climb once it passes ~75%.

runbook.title: Restarts buy time, they don't fix
runbook.detail: Restarting resets the heap but the leak comes straight back. Use it to stabilise while you roll back.

runbook.title: Don't chase the loudest alert
runbook.detail: Slow DB queries can be a symptom: GC-paused pods hold connections longer.

runbook.title: Roll back first, debug later
runbook.detail: If the timing points at a deploy, roll back. You can find the leak in staging tomorrow.

expert_path.why: p99 doubling with no traffic change is worth a name.
Heap slope started exactly at the v2.14.0 marker. Roll back, ask questions later.
Optional: stabilises the pods while the rollback rolls out.
Support was already hearing from customers.

pitfalls.text: More pods spread the load, so each leaks slower, but they all still leak. You delayed the cliff and paid for it.
The slow-query alert was a symptom: paused pods held DB connections longer. There was no missing index.

lessons: Correlate with change first. Deploy markers are the cheapest signal you have.
GC trouble looks like everything else: slow DB, high CPU, timeouts. The heap slope is the tell.
A restart that 'fixes' things for 5 minutes is evidence, not a fix.
debrief.senior_note: I restarted pods three times over a night before anyone looked at the deploy timeline. The fourth on-call rolled back in two minutes.
